original.target_description: Title and DOI verified in the supplied cached primary paper. New locator p. 15 identifies Table 8, hierarchical linear regressions of individual tokens invested in bandwidth. It reports three treatment columns (2 persons, 5 persons, and 5 persons (b)), with separate coefficients for lagged downloading share, its interaction with position, position, and round, plus variance-component tests. The locator does not identify a coefficient/test or treatment; study and outcome description remain absent. Thus the target sample and test cannot be uniquely matched.

replication.target_description: Author report at supplied OSF file verified against Janssen et al. (2011) and project title at referenced OSF node p9k76. It highlights the lagged share by position interaction in the mixed-effects investment regression (Table 3), with alternative specifications in Table 4. No assigned locator, description, or study identifier establishes which reported effect belongs to audit_id 2094.

n.location: p. 3, Table 3, Replication column, Observations and Groups
n.sample_role: Individual investment observations in the critical mixed-effects regression; 14 groups. Table 1 separately reports 70 subjects.
n.exclusions: Practice rounds outside main ten rounds. Printed model N=630. Undefined lagged shares in 20 observations set to 0.2 and retained. Full omission accounting not explicitly reported.

es.location: p. 3, Table 3, Lagged share × position, Replication column

p.location: p. 3, Results continuation for focal interaction; Table 3 notes

reported_success.quote: The replication of the research claim of Janssen et al. (2011) was successful.

notes:
Both full primary papers were acquired and titles verified; neither is unavailable. Input locators_o and locators_r are empty, description and study identifiers are null, and es_type is only ser_method. Following the empty-locator rule, no target-specific statistic or analytic sample was selected. The report identifies its focal claim, but assigning that claim to this audit effect would require an unsupported choice without an input locator. Reported success is the author's overall narrative verdict on that claim, not an independently inferred target-test verdict. Original source: OpenAlex best_oa_location, Indiana University repository publisher-formatted PDF. Replication source: supplied OSF a6nsp/download PDF; OSF node lookup for a6nsp returned 404 because this is a file, while referenced project p9k76 title matched. No numerical conversions performed. Locator-enriched revisit: examined the newly supplied original locator p. 15 (PDF page 15, Table 8). It narrows the original to individual investment regressions but does not specify a treatment column or coefficient/test. Multiple analytic Ns and tests remain possible, so original remains locator_insufficient with null statistics rather than selecting one without support. The Table 8 caption labels bracketed entries p values, although several exceed 1; no bracketed entry was adopted as a p value. Replication locator remains empty, so that side was not revisited. Previously completed author verdict and replication record preserved unchanged. No acquisition attempted and no unchanged paper miss retried.
Completion source review (n_r): Critical model explicitly prints 630 observations and 14 groups. These are observations, not the 70 participating subjects. No sum or df derivation. Twenty undefined lagged shares were set to 0.2 and retained; other model omissions not fully accounted for.
Completion source review (es_value_r): Results explicitly names lagged share × position as the research claim checked, establishing target independently of blank replication locator. Printed coefficient 4.524, SE 0.477. Preserve printed regression coefficient; standardized metric ser_method not established and no conversion made.
Completion source review (pval_value_r): Direct prose reports p < 0.01 for the same focal interaction. Preserve bound; overall model Wald p=.000 is a different test.
Completion source review (reported_success): Author explicitly reports successful replication. Underlying primary report matches assigned URL and original-work identity; author/date differ from catalog-style ref_r and are recorded in checkpoint notes.
